paragraphs: KinderCare Learning Companies, Inc. (the "Company," "KinderCare," "we," "us" and "our") is a leading private provider of high-quality early education and child care services ("ECE") in the United States. We are a mission-driven organization, rooted in a commitment to providing all children with the very best start in life. We serve children ranging from six weeks to 12 years of age across our footprint.

We operate a national network of community-based centers, employer-sponsored programs and before- and after-school sites. Our proprietary curriculum is supported by third-party assessment tools that measure school readiness outcomes. We voluntarily pursue national accreditation at our centers and onsite programs.

We report on a 52- or 53-week fiscal year comprised of 13- or 14-week fourth quarters, respectively, with the fiscal year ending on the Saturday closest to December 31. Our fiscal 2025 was a 53-week year ending on January 3, 2026. References in this Annual Report on Form 10-K to financial or operational results for fiscal 2025 refer to our fiscal year ending January 3, 2026.
We compete in the U.S. market for ECE services, including before- and after-school services for school-aged children.

The market for center-based ECE services is highly fragmented according to Child Care Aware of America. We estimate that the top five providers, including KinderCare, represented approximately 6% of total capacity as of January 3, 2026.
We are a leader in early childhood education and care across our three consumer-facing brands designed to address key parent demographics:

• KinderCare Learning Centers ("KCLC") is a leading provider of community-based early child care and education in the United States. As of January 3, 2026 KCLC operated 1,555 centers with a capacity to serve approximately 200,000 children, of which 77 are employer-based centers. In fiscal 2025 we opened 44 KCLC centers through green fields and acquisitions and closed 18 KCLC centers. KCLC comprised 88% of fiscal 2025 revenue.

• Crème School is a premium provider of community-based early child care and education with 46 schools across 15 states and a capacity for serving over 10,000 children as of January 3, 2026. Crème School is differentiated by its early education model that keeps children stimulated and excited to learn through enrichment programs such as S.T.E.M. Lab, Art Studio, Digital Tech Lab and more. Crème School comprised 4% of fiscal 2025 revenue.

• Champions is a leading private provider of before- and after-school programs for children ages 5-12 in the United States, which also includes summer camp programs. Our outsourced model provides an attractive value proposition to schools and districts. We provide staff, teachers and curriculum to deliver high-quality supplemental education and care at 1,153 sites as of January 3, 2026. Champions comprised 8% of fiscal 2025 revenue.

Additionally, we provide customized family care benefits for organizations, including care for young children on or near the site where their parents work, tuition benefits, and backup care where KinderCare programs are located. Employers increasingly recognize the benefits of offering employees access to flexible, high-quality, affordable ECE options through either a tuition benefits program or as backup care. We believe long-term trends and evolving work styles are driving a preference for flexible ECE solutions with care options both on-site at corporate offices and in the communities in which employees live.

As of January 3, 2026, we operated 77 onsite employer-sponsored centers and had relationships with over 1,000 employers. Our ability to offer both onsite centers, as well as access to our network of programs, provides flexibility and accessibility to a broad range of employees.

Our operating strategy is designed to deliver a high-quality, outcomes-driven, education experience for every child and family we serve across all our centers and sites. This self-reinforcing strategy is anchored in four pillars:

• Educational Excellence. We leverage our proprietary curriculum combined with third-party assessment tools and voluntary accreditation to deliver a high-quality educational experience and provide objective validation of the quality and impact of our programs.

• People & Engagement. We utilize a proprietary, data-driven approach to attract, hire and develop exceptional talent. Our internal surveys consistently demonstrate that a more engaged workforce leads to better financial performance of our centers.

paragraphs: Investing in our common stock involves risks. You should carefully consider the risks described below, together with all of the other information included in this Annual Report, including our consolidated financial statements and related notes included in Item 8 of this Annual Report, before making an investment decision. Our business, financial condition and results of operations could be materially and adversely affected by any of these risks or uncertainties. In that case, the trading price of shares of our common stock could decline, and you may lose all or part of your investment. The risks and uncertainties described below are not the only ones we face. Additional risks and uncertainties that we are unaware of or that we currently see as immaterial may also adversely affect our business.

We serve families and their children six weeks to 12 years of age across the United States and a broad range of demographics and income levels. The success of our business depends on our ability to attract and retain families in our centers, schools and programs. Our marketing efforts may not be successful in attracting families or in attracting employers that provide family care benefits to their workforce. Enrollment levels may materially decline over time.

We experience attrition and must continually engage existing families and attract new families in order to maintain enrollment levels in our centers, sites and programs. Similarly, we must continually engage with existing employers and promote the value of and utilization of our family care benefits by their workforce, maintain renewals of employer contracts, and attract new employers in order to maintain onsite employer-sponsored centers and relationships. Maintaining and growing our enrollment also requires that we develop new consumer-oriented strategies or services to accommodate changing client, children or parent expectations and preferences around service delivery. Our future success depends on our ability to continue to meet the evolving needs and expectations of our clients, including enhancing our existing services.

Employers whose employee base does not regularly use our family care benefits may be more likely to decrease or cancel their arrangements with us. Our contracts with employers for full-service center-based and site-based child care generally have terms of 10 to 15 years, though some have terms as long as 30 years, with varying terms and renewal and termination options. Because of the longer term nature of our contracts with employers, we may experience greater challenges in securing new employers. Employer sponsors have historically reduced their expenditures for benefits related to family services during economic downturns. The termination or non-renewal of a significant number of contracts or the termination of a multiple-site or multiple-service client relationship could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition, results of operations or cash flows.

Families may cancel their enrollment at any time after giving proper notification, in accordance with the terms of their agreement. We may also cancel or suspend enrollment or family care benefits if a family or employer, respectively, fails to provide payment.

Some of the factors that could lead to a decline in enrollment levels include changing demographics of families, their perception of our brand, a shift to remote work, changes in spending trends among families and employers, and general economic conditions, such as inflation, changes in customer behavior as a result of public health or other concerns, market maturity or saturation, a decline in our ability to deliver quality service at a competitive price, increases in tuition rates or the cost of our services, direct and indirect competition in our industry and a decline in families' interest in non-family child care, among other factors. paragraphs: The following discussion and analysis should be read in conjunction with, and is qualified in its entirety by reference to, our audited consolidated financial statements and notes thereto for the fiscal year ended January 3, 2026 included in Item 8 of this Annual Report on Form 10-K. This discussion and analysis primarily addresses the 53-week fiscal year ended January 3, 2026 ("fiscal 2025") and the 52-week fiscal year ended December 28, 2024 ("fiscal 2024") and comparisons between these years. Discussion and analysis as well as comparisons of the fiscal years ended December 28, 2024 and December 30, 2023 can be found within "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations" in our previous Annual Report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 28, 2024 filed with the SEC on March 21, 2025. Some of the information included in this discussion and analysis or set forth elsewhere in this Annual Report on Form 10-K, including information with respect to our plans and strategy for our business, includes forward-looking statements that involve risks and uncertainties. You should review the "Cautionary Note Regarding Forward-Looking Statements" and "Risk Factors" sections included elsewhere in this Annual Report on Form 10-K for a discussion of important factors that could cause actual results to differ materially from the results described in or implied by the forward-looking statements contained in the following discussion and analysis.

KinderCare Learning Companies, Inc. is a leading provider of high-quality ECE in the United States. We are a mission-driven organization, rooted in a commitment to providing all children with the very best start in life. We serve children ranging from six weeks to 12 years of age across our market-leading footprint of 1,601 early childhood education centers with center capacity for 214,803 children and 1,153 before- and after-school sites located in 41 states and the District of Columbia as of January 3, 2026.

On October 8, 2024, our registration statement on Form S-1, as amended (File No. 333-281971) ("Form S-1") related to our IPO, was declared effective by the SEC, and our IPO was completed on October 10, 2024. In connection with our IPO, the Company converted Class A and Class B common stock, both with a par value of $0.0001 per share, to common stock, with a par value of $0.01 per share, at a ratio of 8.375 shares of Class A and Class B common stock to one share of common stock, which became effective immediately following the effectiveness of our registration statement on Form S-1 for our IPO ("Common Stock Conversion"). As a result, prior periods presented in our consolidated financial statements and notes thereto as of and for the fiscal year ended January 3, 2026 have been adjusted to retrospectively reflect the Common Stock Conversion. Refer to Note 17 within the consolidated financial statements included in Item 8 of this Annual Report on Form 10-K for further information.

As a result of certain factors, our historical results of operations may not be comparable from period to period and may not be comparable to our financial results of operations in future periods. Set forth below is a brief discussion of the key factors impacting the comparability of our results of operations.

We report on a 52- or 53-week fiscal year comprised of 13- or 14-week fourth quarters, respectively, with the fiscal year ending on the Saturday closest to December 31. Fiscal 2025 is a 53-week fiscal year as compared to fiscal 2024 which is a 52-week fiscal year. The 53rd week in fiscal 2025 contributed an additional $45.1 million of revenue and an estimated $12 million of adjusted EBITDA.

In October 2024, we sold 27.6 million shares of our common stock through our IPO, including 3.6 million shares sold pursuant to the underwriters' exercise in full of their option to purchase additional shares. Net proceeds of $616.1 million, after underwriting discounts and offering costs, were recognized within additional paid-in capital on the consolidated financial statements. These net proceeds were primarily utilized to repay $608.0 million of outstanding principal on our first lien term loan ("First Lien Term Loan Facility"), which provided us the ability to enter into a refinancing amendment to the credit agreement, dated as of June 12, 2023 (as subsequently amended and restated) (the "Credit Agreement") to reduce the interest rates on our senior secured credit facilities. We recognized a loss on extinguishment of debt of $24.8 million within interest expense as a result of the partial repayment and refinancing of our senior secured credit facilities.

In conjunction with our IPO, we modified the terms of our stock-based award plans. The 2022 Incentive Award Plan ("2022 Plan") was amended to provide for share settlement of all unexercised stock options and unvested restricted stock units ("RSUs") when stock options are exercised and RSUs vest according to their original vesting schedules. As a result of this modification, the previously liability-classified stock options and RSUs were reclassified as equity and the awards will not be remeasured at fair value each reporting period. The 2015 Equity Incentive Plan ("PIUs Plan") was modified to accelerate the vesting of all outstanding profit interest units ("PIUs"). As certain PIUs were improbable to vest prior to the modification and became probable to vest subsequent to the modification, we recognized the full fair value of the awards at the date of modification. As a result of the modification, we recognized $113.1 million as stock-based compensation expense within selling, general, and administrative expenses. The PIUs were settled in shares of our common stock in accordance with the plan of dissolution and liquidation of our parent company effectively terminating the PIUs Plan.

Our IPO, as well as the transactions we entered into in connection with our IPO, have affected the comparability of our operating results for the periods presented. Refer to Note 12 and Note 17 within the consolidated financial statements included in Item 8 of this Annual Report on Form 10-K for further information.

During 2020 and 2021, the United States government approved several incremental stimulus funding programs for ECE providers in response to the coronavirus disease 2019 ("COVID-19") pandemic, and as a result, we have received grants in the form of revenue or cost reimbursements ("COVID-19 Related Stimulus"). We recognized $0.7 million and $63.3 million during fiscal 2025 and fiscal 2024, respectively, in funding for reimbursement of center operating expenses in cost of services (excluding depreciation and impairment). The federal programs funding the COVID-19 Related Stimulus were required to distribute all stimulus funding by December 31, 2024, and we do not expect to receive a material amount of funding after that date. The variability of funding provided by COVID-19 Related Stimulus has impacted the comparability of our operating results for the periods presented.

The Employee Retention Credit ("ERC"), established by the Coronavirus Aid, Relief and Economic Security Act and extended and expanded by several subsequent governmental acts, allows eligible businesses to claim a per employee payroll tax credit based on a percentage of qualified wages, including health care expenses, paid during calendar year 2020 through September 2021. During fiscal 2022, we applied for ERC for qualified wages and benefits paid throughout fiscal 2021 and fiscal 2020. Reimbursements of $62.0 million in cash tax refunds for ERC claimed, along with $2.3 million in interest income, were received during fiscal 2023. Due to the unprecedented nature of ERC legislation and the changing administrative guidance, not all of the ERC reimbursements received have met our recognition criteria. During fiscal 2025 and fiscal 2024, we recognized $30.1 million and $23.4 million of ERC in cost of services (excluding depreciation and impairment), along with $1.3 million and $0.5 million in interest income, respectively. The timing in recognition of the remaining deferred ERC liabilities will have an impact on the comparability of future periods.

We measure and track the number of centers and sites because, as our number of centers and sites grow, it highlights our geographic expansion and potential growth in revenue. We believe this information is useful to investors as an indicator of revenue growth and operational expansion and can be used to measure and track our performance over time. We define the number of centers and sites as the number of centers and sites at the beginning of the period plus openings and acquisitions, minus any permanent closures for the period. A permanently closed center or site is a center or site that has ceased operations as of the end of the reporting period that management does not intend on reopening. During fiscal 2025, management updated the definition of total before- and after-school sites to include sites that are temporarily closed as a result of the summer season to more accurately reflect the total sites that were operating during the year. Prior periods presented were adjusted to reflect the updated definition for comparative purposes.

paragraphs: KinderCare Learning Companies, Inc. (the "Company," "KinderCare," "we," "us" and "our") 為美國領先的私人機構，提供高品質的早期教育與兒童照護服務 ("ECE")。我們為一個以使命為導向的組織，根植於對所有兒童提供最佳人生起點的承諾。我們服務的年齡範圍為出生六週至十二歲的兒童，遍及我們的服務範圍。
我們運作一個全國性的社區中心網路、僱主贊助計畫以及課前與課後服務場所。我們的專利課程由第三方評估工具支援，用以衡量學前教育的準備成果。我們自願性地追求全國認證，以我們的中心與現場計畫為目標。
我們採用 52 或 53 週的財務年度，包含 13 或 14 週的第四季，財務年度結束於最接近 12 月 31 日的星期六。我們的財務 2025 年為 53 週財務年度，結束於 2026 年 1 月 3 日。本年度報表 (Form 10-K) 中提及的財務或營運結果，指的是我們 2025 年財務年度，結束於 2026 年 1 月 3 日。
我們在美國市場與其他 ECE 服務機構競爭，包括為學齡兒童提供的課前與課後服務。
根據 Child Care Aware of America 的資料，以中心為基礎的 ECE 服務市場高度分散。我們估計，包括 KinderCare 在內的前五大服務提供者，截至 2026 年 1 月 3 日，約佔總容量的 6%。
我們在三個面對消費者品牌中，為早期兒童教育與照護的領導者，這些品牌針對關鍵父母族羣設計：

• KinderCare Learning Centers ("KCLC") 為美國領先的社區為基礎的早期兒童照護與教育服務提供者。截至 2026 年 1 月 3 日，KCLC 運作 1,555 個中心，服務容量約為 200,000 名兒童，其中 77 個為僱主為基礎的中心。在 2025 財務年度，我們透過新開設與收購方式開設 44 個 KCLC 中心，並關閉 18 個 KCLC 中心。KCLC 佔據 2025 財務年度營業收入的 88%。

• Crème School 為社區為基礎的高階早期兒童照護與教育服務提供者，在 15 個州運作 46 所學校，截至 2026 年 1 月 3 日，服務容量超過 10,000 名兒童。Crème School 的特色在於其早期教育模式，透過豐富的課程如 S.T.E.M. 實驗室、藝術工作室、數位科技實驗室等，激發兒童學習的興趣與熱情。Crème School 佔據 2025 財務年度營業收入的 4%。
• Champions 是美國提供 5 至 12 歲兒童課前及課後教育與照顧服務的領導性私人機構，服務項目亦包含暑期營隊。我們的委外模式為學校與學區提供具吸引力的價值主張。我們提供員工、教師與課程，於 2026 年 1 月 3 日為止的 1,153 個場地提供高品質的補充教育與照顧服務。Champions 佔 2025 財年營業收入的 8%。

此外，我們為機構提供客製化的家庭照顧福利，包括在父母工作地點附近照顧年幼子女、學費補助以及在 KinderCare 程式所在地提供備用照顧服務。僱主越來越認同提供員工接取彈性、高品質、可負擔的 ECE（早期兒童教育）選項的效益，透過學費補助計畫或作為備用照顧服務。我們認為長期趨勢與工作方式的演變，正驅動員工偏好具有彈性的 ECE 解決方案，包含企業辦公室內的現場照顧服務以及員工居住社區的照顧選項。
截至 2026 年 1 月 3 日，我們運作 77 個企業贊助的現場中心，並與超過 1,000 家僱主有合作關係。我們能提供現場中心以及接入我們程式網路的服務，為廣泛的員工提供彈性與可近性。
本公司營運策略係設計用以提供高品質、以成果為導向的教育體驗，針對我們所有中心及場地所服務的每個兒童與家庭。此自強不息的策略以四大支柱為基礎：
• 教育卓越。我們運用本公司專屬的課程內容，結合第三方評估工具及自願性認證，以提供高品質的教育體驗，並提供客觀的驗證以確認我們計畫的品質與影響力。
• 人才與參與度。我們採用專屬的數據驅動方法，用以吸引、聘用並培訓卓越人才。我們內部的問卷調查持續顯示，更具參與度的員工團隊會帶來我們中心更佳的財務表現。

paragraphs: 下列討論與分析應與我們經審計之合併財務報表及其附註，並配合閱讀，且完整內容應參照本年度報告表10-K第8項所載之財務報表及附註，財務年度為2026年1月3日結訖。本討論與分析主要針對2025財年（53週財年，結訖於2026年1月3日）及2024財年（52週財年，結訖於2024年12月28日）之財務表現，並比較這兩年間之差異。有關2024財年及2023財年結訖於2024年12月28日及2023年12月30日之財務討論與分析及比較，可於我們2024財年年度報告表10-K中「管理層對財務狀況與營運結果之討論與分析」部分找到。本討論與分析中包含部分資訊，或於本年度報告表10-K其他部分提及，包括有關我們業務計畫與策略之資訊，均包含風險與不確定性之預測性陳述。請審閱本年度報告表10-K中「預測性陳述之警示」及「風險因素」部分，以瞭解可能導致實際結果與預測性陳述中所述或暗示之結果有重大差異的重要因素。
KinderCare Learning Companies, Inc. 是美國高品質早期兒童教育（ECE）之領導供應商。我們是一家以使命為導向之組織，根植於提供所有兒童最佳起點之承諾。我們服務年齡從六週至十二歲之兒童，透過我們市場領先之1,601個早期兒童教育中心，擁有214,803個兒童之中心容量，以及1,153個課後與課前學習場所，分佈於41個州及華盛頓特區，截至2026年1月3日。

2024年10月8日，我們提交之Form S-1註冊聲明（檔案編號333-281971）（"Form S-1"）經美國證券交易委員會（SEC）宣告生效，我們之首次公開發行（IPO）於2024年10月10日完成。配合我們之IPO，本公司將Class A及Class B普通股（每股票面價值為$0.0001）轉換為普通股（每股票面價值為$0.01），轉換比例為8.375股Class A及Class B普通股換取1股普通股，此轉換於我們Form S-1註冊聲明生效後立即生效（"普通股轉換"）。因此，我們合併財務報表及其附註中截至2026年1月3日財務年度之歷史財務資料已回溯調整以反映普通股轉換。有關進一步資訊，請參閱本年度報告表10-K第8項所載合併財務報表中之附註17。
由於某些因素，我們歷史之營運結果可能無法與各期間比較，也可能與未來期間之財務結果無法比較。下列為影響我們營運結果可比性之關鍵因素簡要討論。
我們採用52週或53週財年，包含13週或14週之第四季，財年結訖於最接近12月31日之星期六。2025財年為53週財年，與2024財年（52週財年）相比。2025財年之第53週為我們帶來額外$45.1百萬之營業收入，以及預估$12百萬之調整後EBITDA。

2024年10月，我們透過IPO出售27.6百萬股普通股，包含3.6百萬股為經經紀人行使選擇權後所出售之股數。扣除經紀人折扣及發行費用後，淨資金$616.1百萬已計入合併財務報表之附加資本。這些淨資金主要用於償還$608.0百萬之首優抵押貸款（"First Lien Term Loan Facility"）本金，此貸款使我們得以與信用協議（日期為2023年6月12日，後經修正及重述）（"信用協議"）進行融資協議修正，以降低我們之高階抵押信用貸款之利率。我們因部分償還及重新融資高階抵押信用貸款而認列$24.8百萬之債務消滅損失，計入利息費用。

配合我們之IPO，我們修改了股票獎勵計畫之條款。2022年激勵獎勵計畫（"2022計畫"）已修正，以允許所有未執行之股票選擇權及未解鎖之限制性股票單位（"RSUs"）在股票選擇權執行及RSUs依原解鎖時間表解鎖時，以股票結算。因此，因此修改，原先被歸類為負債之股票選擇權及RSUs已重新歸類為權益，且這些獎勵將不再於每個會計期間重新衡量其公允價值。2015年權益激勵計畫（"PIUs計畫"）已修正，以加速所有現有利潤權益單位（"PIUs"）之解鎖。因某些PIUs在修正前極不可能解鎖，而在修正後成為可能解鎖，我們於修正日認列這些獎勵之完整公允價值。因此修改，我們於銷售、一般及行政費用中認列$113.1百萬之股票獎勵費用。PIUs依解散及清算計畫以我們普通股股票結算，此計畫實際上終止了PIUs計畫。
我們之IPO，以及我們配合IPO所進行之交易，已影響我們所呈現期間之營運結果可比性。有關進一步資訊，請參閱本年度報告表10-K第8項所載合併財務報表中之附註12及附註17。

2020 年及 2021 年，美國政府針對 ECE 提供者批准了數個增量的紓困資金計畫，以應對冠狀病毒疾病 2019（"COVID-19"）疫情，因此，我們已收到以收入或成本補償形式的補助金（"COVID-19 相關紓困"）。我們在財務年度 2025 認列 0.7 百萬美元，以及財務年度 2024 認列 63.3 百萬美元，用以補償中心營運費用的資金，包含在服務成本中（扣除折舊及減損）。提供 COVID-19 相關紓困的聯邦計畫要求於 2024 年 12 月 31 日前發放所有紓困資金，我們不預期在該日期之後會收到重大金額的資金。COVID-19 相關紓困所提供的資金變動性已影響我們所呈現期間的營運結果可比性。

員工保留信用（"ERC"），由冠狀病毒援助、 Relief 及經濟安全法案建立，並經多項後續政府法案延長及擴展，允許符合資格的企業根據合格工資（包括醫療費用）的百分比，申報每名員工的薪資稅抵減。在財務年度 2022，我們為財務年度 2021 及 2020 全年所支付的合格工資及福利申報 ERC。在財務年度 2023，我們收到 62.0 百萬美元現金稅退款補償及 2.3 百萬美元利息收入。由於 ERC 法規的前所未有的性質及行政指引的變動，並非所有 ERC 補償金額都符合我們的認列標準。在財務年度 2025 及 2024，我們分別認列 30.1 百萬美元及 23.4 百萬美元 ERC 在服務成本中（扣除折舊及減損），以及 1.3 百萬美元及 0.5 百萬美元利息收入。剩餘遞延 ERC 應付義務的認列時間將影響未來期間的可比性。

我們衡量並追蹤中心及場地數量，因為隨著我們的中心及場地數量增加，這突顯了我們的地理擴張及潛在收入成長。我們認為這項資訊對投資者而言是有用的，作為收入成長及營運擴張的指標，也可用來衡量及追蹤我們的表現。我們將中心及場地數量定義為期初的中心及場地數量，加上新開設及收購的數量，扣除該期間任何永久關閉的數量。永久關閉的中心或場地是指截至報表期間結束時已停止營運，且管理層不預計重新開幕的中心或場地。在財務年度 2025，管理層更新了總計前後學童場地的定義，以包含因暑假而暫時關閉的場地，以更準確反映該年度實際營運的總計場地數量。先前期間的資料已調整以反映更新後的定義，以供比較用途。
截至 2026 年 1 月 3 日，我們擁有 1,601 個早期兒童教育中心，中心容量可服務 214,803 名兒童，與截至 2024 年 12 月 28 日的 1,574 個早期兒童教育中心相比，當時的中心容量可服務 210,135 名兒童。在財務年度 2025，總計中心數量增加 27 個，這是因為收購 26 個中心及開設 20 個中心，部分抵銷 19 個永久關閉的中心。

headings: 與我們業務相關的風險
我們的成敗取決於我們吸引並留住中心、學校及 programme 中的家庭，以及吸引並留住與我們簽約提供員工家庭照護福利的僱主之能力。
我們的業務 largely 取決於我們聘僱並留住合格教師，並維持強大員工參與度之能力。
我們依賴關鍵管理階層及關鍵員工來管理我們的業務。
由於我們的成敗 substantially 取決於我們品牌價值及作為首選服務提供者的聲譽，不利的公眾意見可能影響我們服務的需求。
我們產業中顯著的競爭可能不利地影響我們的營運結果。
我們的獲利能力取決於我們管理勞動成本之能力。
我們能否取得可負擔的實體租賃及在可接受條款下續約現有租賃，可能影響我們的營運結果。
本公司對第三方廠商及服務供應商之依賴，使我們面臨可能不利影響業務之營運及成本風險。
本公司營運成果會受到季節性波動之影響。
本公司業務可能因聯邦資助之兒少照顧補貼或學費補償延遲、中斷或減少，或因某些聯邦、州及地方政府計畫減少而受到影響。
政府推行之全民兒少照顧福利計畫，可能降低對本公司服務之需求。
併購會帶來許多風險，並可能幹擾本公司營運。本公司亦可能無法實現交易當時預期之財務及戰略目標。
公共衛生危機及廣泛傳播之健康大流行或疫情，在過去曾且可能未來繼續對本公司業務、財務狀況及營運成果造成不利影響。
本公司業務、財務狀況及營運成果可能因各種訴訟及監管程序而受到重大且不利影響。
與本公司負債、資本需求及資本結構相關之風險
我們可能需要額外資金以履行財務義務並支持業務成長，且此資金可能無法在可接受的條件或完全無法取得。
本公司為一控股公司，本身無任何營運活動，並依賴子公司提供現金。
保險覆蓋不足或無法取得契約所要求的保險 coverage 可能對本公司業務、財務狀況及營運成果產生重大且不利的影響。
商譽、其他無形資產或長壽命資產的減損已對我們的營運成果產生負面影響，並可能在未來繼續產生負面影響。
與智慧財產權、資訊科技及資料隱私權與安全性相關的風險
若我們無法充分保護智慧財產權，將可能對本公司業務、財務狀況及營運成果產生重大且不利的影響。
paragraphs: 投資本公司的普通股涉及風險。您應仔細考慮下列所描述的風險，並配合本年度報告中包含的所有其他資訊，包括本年度報告第 8 項所載的合併財務報表及相關附註，再做投資決定。本公司業務、財務狀況及營運成果可能因任何這些風險或不確定性而受到重大且不利的影響。在此情況下，本公司普通股的交易價格可能下跌，您可能損失全部或部分投資。下列所描述的風險與不確定性並非本公司所面臨的唯一風險。我們可能還會面臨其他我們未察覺或目前認為不重要的風險與不確定性，這些也可能對本公司業務造成不利影響。
我們服務美國六歲至十二歲的兒童及其家庭，並涵蓋廣泛的族羣與收入層次。本公司業務的成功取決於我們吸引並留住家庭在中心、學校及計畫中的能力。我們的行銷努力可能無法成功吸引家庭，或吸引提供家庭照顧福利的僱主。入學人數可能隨時間大幅下降。

我們會經歷人員流失，必須持續與現有家庭互動並吸引新家庭，以維持中心、場地及計畫中的入學人數。同樣地，我們必須持續與現有僱主互動，促進其工作人員對我們家庭照顧福利的使用價值，維持僱主契約的續約，並吸引新僱主，以維持場內僱主贊助的中心與關係。維持並擴大我們的入學人數，也要求我們發展新的消費者導向策略或服務，以因應客戶、兒童或家長在服務交付方面的變動需求與偏好。我們未來的成功取決於我們持續滿足客戶變動的需求與期望，包括提升我們現有的服務。

那些員工不常使用我們家庭照顧福利的僱主，可能更傾向減少或取消與我們的安排。我們與僱主的全服務中心基於或場地基於兒童照顧契約，通常有 10 到 15 年的期限，雖然有些契約的期限可達 30 年，並有不同條款及續約與終止選項。由於我們與僱主的契約具有較長的期限，我們可能在尋找新僱主時遇到更大困難。僱主贊助者在經濟衰退期間，歷來會減少與家庭服務相關的福利支出。若終止或未續約大量契約，或終止多場地或多服務的客戶關係，可能對本公司業務、財務狀況、營運成果或現金流造成重大不利影響。
家庭可在依契約條款給予適當通知後，隨時取消入學。我們也可能因家庭或僱主未支付費用，而取消或暫停入學或家庭照顧福利。

導致入學人數下降的一些因素包括家庭人口結構的變化、對我們品牌的看法、遠距工作的趨勢、家庭與僱主的支出趨勢變化，以及總體經濟狀況，例如通貨膨脹、因公共衛生或其他因素導致的客戶行為變化、市場成熟或飽和、我們在競爭性價格下提供優質服務能力的下降、學費率或我們服務成本的提高、我們產業中的直接與間接競爭，以及家庭對非家庭兒童照顧興趣的下降，等等。若我們未能成功優化學費率，或在新舊中心、場地及計畫中增加新入學人數，或增加新僱主，成長營收可能受影響
